result:
Before I write it up, there's one bigger choice to settle: how the whole guide gets built, not just how the recordings are handled. Your current site is static pages on Netlify, and those can't take uploads on their own. So something new is needed whichever way we go.

1. **Build it into the museum's existing website.** Each exhibit gets a guide page, and its code links there. The page plays the story in the visitor's chosen language and remembers the choice on their phone. Volunteers log into a simple editing screen added to the site, pick an exhibit and language, and upload their recording. The site cleans up the audio each time it rebuilds.
   - For: one place to look after, no new accounts or hosting bills, and it uses the tools the site already runs on.
   - Against: a new recording takes a few minutes to go live, while the site rebuilds.

2. **Use a hosted audio-guide service.** These platforms already offer codes, playback and uploads.
   - For: almost nothing to build.
   - Against: a monthly fee, and you're limited to what they offer. Welsh support and automatic cleanup may not be there, and your stories live on someone else's platform.

3. **A separate small web app with its own database and file storage.** Uploads would go live instantly, and it has room to grow.
   - For: the most flexible of the three.
   - Against: it's a second system to host, secure and pay for, which is a lot for sixty stories and ten new ones a year.

I recommend **1**. It fits how rarely things change, keeps volunteers to one simple screen, and adds nothing new for the museum to maintain.

This is a project-sized piece of work, so the design will be a full written document saved alongside the website. A reviewer will read it before I hand it over, and I may come back once with a few questions.

Shall I go with option 1? Or would you prefer one of the others?
